scope: Storage comparison; load, validation and maintenance jobs can overlap, so their timings are diagnostic rather than a controlled throughput comparison.
method: Fresh equal-data databases; sum all regular database-file bytes including indexes, metadata and locks; allocated totals independently checked against du -s -B1; no WAL files remain after close. Before/after sizes are captured serially on task-created databases.
durability: WAL enabled and WAL fsync disabled for new loads. DuckDB uses the existing Linux shim restricted to its exact WAL file. Other DuckDB and SlopDB checkpoint/SSTable/MANIFEST syncing stays enabled. File allocation is recorded after syncing closed files.

engines.wal_fsync_mode: Linux preload bypass restricted to this database WAL; other files remain synced

tpcc.generation: Replicate one committed snapshot into disjoint warehouse ranges; shift w_id, c_w_id and supply_w_id by replica*2, shift history h_id by replica*(source max h_id+1); keep the 1000-item catalog shared. Repeated source values can affect compression. This is an equal-data storage snapshot, not a new timed TPC-C transaction run.
tpcc.validation: Compare every column of every row after reopen and after maintenance; bounded primary-key queries use >= and <=, ORDER BY primary key, and LIMIT expected rows+1. Total table counts must match exactly.
